matches.rationale: GT1 concerns a fabricated reference [39] about adaptive temporal windowing in the Introduction. None of the findings identify a fabricated citation or reference issue.

GT2 identifies a logical inconsistency in Equation (4) regarding mixing raw scores with softmax probabilities. Pred_3 identifies an arithmetic error in a different equation about time steps. These are distinct issues.

GT3 describes contradictory data split information (8.5 years training, testing 2015) and filtering of high MAE points. Pred_1 explicitly identifies the filtering issue, and Pred_2 identifies the contradictory training/testing periods across sections. Both findings capture the experimental design protocol corruption.
GT4 concerns the exaggerated 'first' claim in the Abstract about six-hourly forecasting. None of the findings address this specific claim distortion in the Abstract.

GT5 identifies implausibly large performance margins in Figure 4 suggesting cherry-picking or metric manipulation. None of the findings specifically address Figure 4 or this performance exaggeration issue.
GT6 concerns rhetorical exaggeration in the Conclusion omitting limitations. None of the findings identify issues specifically in the Conclusion section's rhetoric.

GT7 identifies inconsistency between claims about multi-step loss mitigating error accumulation versus observed error growth in figures. None of the findings address this method-results inconsistency.
GT8 concerns the omission of uncertainty quantification and confidence intervals in the Experiments section. None of the findings identify this ethical transparency issue.
GT9 identifies unexplained reduction from 40 vertical layers (5,000m) to 20 layers (1,500m) in Section 4.1. None of the findings address this vertical layer inconsistency.

GT10 identifies questionable salinity error values and inconsistent axis labels/scales in Figures 3 and 5. Pred_4 explicitly states 'units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges' in Section 5.3, matching this data integrity issue.
GT11 concerns rhetorical exaggeration ('superior skill', 'state-of-the-art') in the Abstract. None of the findings identify this specific rhetorical manipulation in the Abstract.
GT12 identifies insufficient discussion of reanalysis data bias risks in the Appendix. None of the findings address this ethical omission regarding training data limitations.
GT13 concerns selective presentation in Figure 2 spatial error maps emphasizing low-error regions. None of the findings identify this biased presentation of spatial errors.
GT14 identifies the problematic batch size of 1 per GPU (effective batch size 4) as an unreported design choice. None of the findings address this training configuration issue.

GT15 identifies mismatch between training data (2006-2014) and comparison models trained on later data (2020-2021) per Table 1. Pred_2 identifies contradictions between Section 4.1 and Table 1 regarding data periods, capturing this context misalignment.
GT16 concerns overgeneralization in the Conclusion about 6-hour forecast effectiveness across all variables. None of the findings identify this claim distortion in the Conclusion.

GT17 identifies rhetorical downplaying of errors in western boundary currents using 'operational tolerance thresholds' language. None of the findings address this specific rhetorical manipulation in the Experiments section.
